capex_override.ack_reason: The out-of-band flag is mechanical only: the band is computed against the last FILED capex value under an engine-read tag, which is the FY2020 PaymentsToAcquireOtherPropertyPlantAndEquipment fact of $8,308,000 — a minor equipment line, not the filer's real-estate capex line at all (AHR's actual capex is filed only as 'Developments and capital expenditures', per the source). The override is not an estimate lacking an anchor — it is the median of the filer's own FY2023-25 cash-flow figures from its FY2025 10-K.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because AHR reports its real-estate capex only as the combined cash-flow line 'Developments and capital expenditures' (ISHC development/expansion plus recurring property capex), which no engine candidate tag carries; the small PaymentsToAcquireOtherPropertyPlantAndEquipment series the engine does read ends at FY2020. The engine applies this single value to every missing period; it is the median of the three filed years. Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2024 capex by $7,851,000 (conservative direction — lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $28,771,000 (flatters the latest year; noted, not hidden — the TTM pin used for the base charges the same $99,791,000 against TTM OCF, below FY2025's filed $128,562,000 run rate, so the base is if anything generous on capex). 'Acquisitions of real estate investments' ($884,425,000 in FY2025, same statement) is excluded: it is property M&A presented separately by the filer, not capex.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-27, accession 0001193125-26-082692), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Developments and capital expenditures': $(99,791) thousand for FY2023, $(91,940) thousand for FY2024 and $(128,562) thousand for FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2023 figure). The same 10-K (Note 3, Real Estate Investments) reports capital expenditures incurred by segment of $100,971k / $87,562k / $143,103k for FY2023/24/25; the cash-flow line is used because the engine's capex is a cash concept.

moat_against: Real estate is replicable with capital — no network effects, no lock-in beyond leases; location advantages are local and contestable
Measured returns falling: ROIC proxy 19.8% (FY2023) → 13.2% (FY2024) → 10.2% (FY2025), and that denominator omits untagged debt, so the true figure is lower

Growth is bought with continuous equity issuance: weighted diluted shares +27.7% in FY2025, 217,998,775 shares outstanding by Aug 2026, ~12.2M forward-sale shares still unsettled — per-share economics lag portfolio growth
RIDEA operating exposure: labor costs, operator concentration (Trilogy in ISHC), and Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement risk in skilled nursing
Short listed history (NYSE listing Feb 2024), no through-cycle record as a public company; CEO Danny Prosky on medical leave during 2026 per the FY2025 10-K
moat_for: RIDEA operating platform (ISHC + SHOP) captures operating upside directly, not just rent — Q2 2026 same-store NOI +16.1% ISHC / +20.5% SHOP, tenth straight double-digit quarter
Structural supply/demand: senior-housing new supply at generational lows while the 80+ cohort grows — occupancy and pricing tailwind
Scale and operator network built over ~20 years (Trilogy platform); 337 buildings / ~22.2M sq ft at FY2025, sourcing off-market deals
Deep access to equity capital at premium prices funds growth and keeps leverage low — net debt / annualized adjusted EBITDA 2.5x at Q2 2026, total indebtedness $1.4B
moat_justification: Weak-moderate 4/10, in line with peer healthcare REITs in this sweep: the RIDEA operating platform, the demographic tailwind and record-low senior-housing new supply give real current pricing power, but the assets are replicable with capital, there is no durable lock-in beyond leases, measured ROIC is falling (roic_proxy 19.8% FY2023 to 10.2% FY2025 in fundamentals.json, on a denominator that omits the debt the engine could not tag, so it flatters), and growth must be continuously bought with dilutive equity issuance.
name: American Healthcare REIT, Inc.
one_liner: Real-estate growth story priced far past its owner's earnings, moat 4/10 — even on the generous TTM base ($1.27/sh) the weighted IRR is 5.8% (weighted IV@15% $13.23 vs the $53.23 price), the entire scenario band is Tier D, and the price would have to fall to ~$13 to clear the 15% hurdle; confidence low (sector model mismatch).
